newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel surges 1.2 pct against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel surges 1.2 pct against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose 1.2 percent against the dollar on Wednesday bringing the currency's gain to a total of 2.4 percent since Friday, dealers said.

"Tuesday's trend continued today. After the setting of the representative rate on Tuesday the shekel continued to rise to 3.53 shekels per dollar. During the day (Wednesday) the shekel continued to rise reaching 3.4980 before it started weakening again," said Guy Levi a dealer at Bank Leumi.
"Activity was lower today and the market is still very nervous. One big buyer or seller can move the whole market," he said.
"The market has got its confidence back in the shekel," said Shiko Angert, a dealer at Union Bank.
The shekel tumbled five percent in the last week of June after the government instituted changes in the exchange rate mechanism and the Bank of Israel slashed interest rates 1.2 percentage points.

Dealers said spreads had narrowed this morning to 30 to 50 points but widened again later in the day to 70-100. "The spreads are still very wide. The market is still nervous," said Ilan Viskin of Bank Hapoalim.

He said the market was too jittery to make any short-term predictions of where the currency would settle, but Angert said he expected the shekel would reach the bottom end of its trading band against the currency basket next week. That, he added, would touch off Bank of Israel intervention.
The basket representative rate was fixed 1.97 percent above the band.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5050 shekels against 3.5490 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7980 against 3.8493 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0625 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0870 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 2.0030 shekels compared with 2.0348 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5180 shekels.
